Real nonlinear conductivity pairs propose exponential sensing barriers and a conditioned finite-shell inverse On B_1 in R^n, n>=3, consider real smooth scalar conductivities in [1/2,3/2], equal to one near the boundary, with integer Sobolev index s>n/2. For a supplied smooth axisymmetric bump psi supported inside B_r away from the rotation axis, the source constructs sigma_k^±=1±a k^-s psi(rho,z) cos(k theta). Their calibrated-coordinate L2 separation is sqrt(2) a ||psi||_2 k^-s, but their nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann response difference in the harmonic-energy operator norm is at most C a k^-s r^k. This is an internally reconstructed proof candidate; quantitative separation modulo a gauge is OPEN.

A rotation pi/k exchanges the two coefficients. Odd nonlinear terms couple angular blocks only across odd multiples of k. The boundary norm is ||f||_E^2=integral |grad Hf|^2=sum_(ell>=1) ell ||f_ell||_2^2 with constants quotiented out; scalar energy readouts or real/imaginary pairings are admitted (a complex pairing costs two real readouts). Interior harmonic energy decays with angular degree, and summing the full operator blocks charges multiplicities. An independent-to-target initial worker and later informed internal reconstruction give alternative energy/resolvent accounts; these are internal campaign checks, not external verification. The Schur-resolvent subtraction cancels all even powers. Linearized invisibility alone is not substituted for a nonlinear bound.

For angular band limit L with 2L<k, allowed boundary pairings coincide exactly. With adversarial absolute readout noise nu and probe energy ||f||_E^2<=Emax, Emax||Delta Lambda||<=2nu supplies a common midpoint adaptive transcript and risk at least half the pair separation. Under the stated independent Gaussian variance-nu^2 model and bounded experiment/stopping contract, the joint random-seed/data KL controls success; marginal data KL is only upper bounded by it. Success probability 3/4 below half separation requires expected sum ||f_j||_E^4 >=nu^2/||Delta Lambda||^2. This does not acquire detector noise, causal delivery or a universal excitation/energy-time law. General discontinuous adaptive policies do not inherit the continuous-transcript quantitative width bound.

The complementary positive result is for D KNOWN nonnegative smooth profiles on ordered disjoint radial shells [a_j,b_j], not arbitrary unknown media. D unit-energy harmonic probes of degrees 1..D give scalar measurements F_l(c). Their background Jacobian M_lj=(2l+n-2) integral phi_j(r) r^(2l+n-3) dr has determinant >=d_*>0 from an averaged Vandermonde formula. B=D/d_* bounds its inverse infinity norm and rho=min{1/2,1/(24B)} bounds the prior radius (further reduced to satisfy the Sobolev ball). For ||c_*||_infinity<=rho/2 and readout error zeta with B zeta<=rho/4, c_(q+1)=c_q+M^-1(y-F(c_q)) contracts and ||c_q-c_*||_infinity<=2^-q||c_*||_infinity+2B zeta. Certified forward error tau must replace zeta by zeta+tau; an inexact matrix inverse also needs an explicit certificate. Thin shells, small gaps and D make conditioning costly. The radial ODE evaluator is specified, not implemented or certified at all accuracies.

Family fit: existing inverse/geometry/identifiability/acquisition topics. Quantum tomography or a supplied continuum uniqueness theorem does not supply this real nonlinear finite-noise interface. No earlier Astra theorem is imported as a premise. Exact priority, gauge-quotient recovery, useful sensing advantage and physical experiment remain UNKNOWN or unperformed.

source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The operational target

Let \(\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^n\), \(n\ge3\). A scalar conductivity \(\sigma\) equals one outside an interior ball \(B_r\), where \(0<r<1\), and obeys \(1/2\le\sigma\le3/2\). A boundary voltage \(f\) produces the weak solution
\[
 \operatorname{div}(\sigma\nabla u_{\sigma,f})=0,
 \qquad u_{\sigma,f}|_{\partial B_1}=f.
\]
The scalar readout is the energy \(Q_\sigma(f)=B_\sigma(f,f)\), or the real/imaginary part of a pairing
\[
 B_\sigma(f,h)=\int_{B_1}\sigma\nabla u_{\sigma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla u_{\sigma,h}}\,dx.
\]
A complex pairing costs two real readouts. This note gives the experiment generous access to all boundary voltages. Every lower bound therefore also applies to voltages supported on a fixed open patch \(\Gamma\).

Use the exact background-energy norm
\[
 \|f\|_E^2=\int_{B_1}|\nabla u_{1,f}|^2dx
 =\sum_{\ell\ge1}\ell\|f_\ell\|_{L^2(S^{n-1})}^2.
\]
Here \(f_\ell\) is the spherical-harmonic component of degree \(\ell\), and constants are quotiented out. This is the homogeneous \(H^{1/2}\) norm. The dissipated energy satisfies
\[
 \tfrac12\|f\|_E^2\le Q_\sigma(f)\le\tfrac32\|f\|_E^2.
\]
Thus this norm charges a physical excitation resource, rather than allowing unbounded high-frequency voltages for free. The requested output is a finite representation of \(\sigma\), with error in \(L^2(B_1)\), in already calibrated Euclidean coordinates.

## 2. Explicit smooth real pair

Write \(x=(\rho\cos\theta,\rho\sin\theta,z)\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{n-2}\). Fix a nonzero, real, rotation-invariant \(\psi\in C_c^\infty(B_r)\), with support separated from the rotation axis \(\{\rho=0\}\), and normalize \(\|\psi\|_\infty\le1\). For an integer \(k\ge1\), integer \(s>n/2\), and \(0<a\le1/2\), put
\[
 h_k(x)=\psi(\rho,z)\cos(k\theta),\qquad
 t_k=ak^{-s},\qquad \sigma_k^\pm=1\pm t_kh_k.
\]
These coefficients are smooth and uniformly elliptic and equal one on a fixed boundary collar. Because the support avoids the axis, differentiation gives
\[
 \|h_k\|_{H^s}\le C_{\psi,s}k^s,
 \qquad \|\sigma_k^\pm-1\|_{H^s}\le C_{\psi,s}a.
\]
The angular integral of \(\cos^2(k\theta)\) is independent of \(k\), so their separation is exactly
\[
 \Delta_k:=\|\sigma_k^+-\sigma_k^-\|_2
 =\sqrt2\,a\|\psi\|_2k^{-s}.                    \tag{1}
\]
Choosing \(a\le\eta/C_{\psi,s}\) puts all of them in any prescribed positive \(H^s\) radius \(\eta\).

## 3. Nonlinear localized-energy estimate

For \(\sigma=1\pm th_k\), \(t\le1/2\), set \(\kappa=1-t\). Write \(u_{\sigma,f}=u_{1,f}+w\), with \(w\in H_0^1(B_1)\). The exact weak equation gives
\[
 \int\sigma\nabla w\cdot\overline{\nabla v}
 =-\int(\sigma-1)\nabla u_{1,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla v}.
\]
Taking \(v=w\), using support in \(B_r\) and coercivity, yields
\[
 \|\nabla w\|_{L^2(B_1)}\le\frac{t}{\kappa}
     \|\nabla u_{1,f}\|_{L^2(B_r)},
 \quad
 \|\nabla u_{\sigma,f}\|_{L^2(B_r)}\le\kappa^{-1}
     \|\nabla u_{1,f}\|_{L^2(B_r)}.                \tag{2}
\]
There is no Born approximation in (2). Alessandrini's exact identity, obtainable by subtracting the two weak equations, now gives for \(D_k=\Lambda_{\sigma_k^+}-\Lambda_{\sigma_k^-}\)
\[
 |\langle D_kf,h\rangle|
 \le\frac{2t_k}{\kappa^2}
 \|\nabla u_{1,f}\|_{L^2(B_r)}
 \|\nabla u_{1,h}\|_{L^2(B_r)}.                 \tag{3}
\]

## 4. Exact angular selection and the full operator bound

Complexify the boundary Hilbert space and decompose it into rotation characters
\[
 E=\widehat\bigoplus_{p\in\mathbb Z}E_p,
 \qquad f_p(R_\alpha x)=e^{ip\alpha}f_p(x).
\]
A degree-\(\ell\) spherical harmonic has only weights \(|p|\le\ell\). For \(f_p\in E_p\), harmonic extension and radial integration give
\[
 \|\nabla u_{1,f_p}\|_{L^2(B_r)}^2
 =\sum_{\ell\ge\max(1,|p|)}\ell r^{2\ell+n-2}
       \|(f_p)_\ell\|_2^2
 \le r^{2|p|+n-2}\|f_p\|_E^2.                \tag{4}
\]
The harmless slack at \(p=0\) avoids a special case.

Rotation by \(\alpha=\pi/k\) exchanges \(\sigma_k^+\) and \(\sigma_k^-\). The covariance of the weak boundary form implies that conjugating \(D_k\) by this rotation changes its sign. Consequently,
\[
 \langle D_kf_p,h_q\rangle=0
 \quad\hbox{unless}\quad p-q\in k(2\mathbb Z+1). \tag{5}
\]
This is an exact selection rule for the nonlinear DN maps. Combining (3)–(5), the norm of a nonzero \((p,q)\) block is at most
\[
 b_{pq}=\frac{2t_k}{\kappa^2}r^{|p|+|q|+n-2}
            {\bf1}_{p-q\in k(2\mathbb Z+1)}.
\]
For every \(p\), the triangle inequality \(|p|+|q|\ge|p-q|\) gives
\[
 \sum_qb_{pq}
 \le\frac{2t_k}{\kappa^2}r^{n-2}
       \sum_{j\in\mathbb Z}r^{|(2j+1)k|}
 =\frac{4t_k}{\kappa^2}
       \frac{r^{k+n-2}}{1-r^{2k}}.
\]
The same bound holds for columns. The Hilbert-space block Schur test (apply the scalar Schur test to \(\|f_p\|_E\)) proves
\[
 \boxed{\|D_k\|_{E\to E^*}
 \le\frac{4t_k}{(1-t_k)^2}

source_excerpts.text:
## 5. Bounded noise: a probe-count-independent precision floor

Consider any deterministic adaptive protocol, allowing even discontinuous choices of the next probe, whose energy inputs satisfy \(\|f_j\|_E^2\le E_{\max}\). Suppose each scalar readout can have arbitrary error \(|e_j|\le\nu\). For a pairing, replace the energy bound by \(\|f_j\|_E\|h_j\|_E\le E_{\max}\). Let \(\delta_k\) denote the right-hand side of (6). If
\[
 E_{\max}\delta_k\le2\nu,                     \tag{8}
\]
the two media admit identical complete transcripts: at each common previous transcript, the next probe is the same; answer its response by the midpoint of the two true values. This answer is within \(\nu\) of both. Thus every reconstruction has worst-case error at least \(\Delta_k/2\), regardless of the number of probes.

For a randomized policy, the same construction yields identical transcript/output distributions when the bounded-error adversary may respond to the actual query. Hence the two disjoint success balls cannot both have probability greater than one half; this is a minimax confidence/expected-risk statement, not a fixed-coefficient pointwise error assertion for every random seed. It does **not** imply that independent centered random noise cannot be averaged away.

For fixed \(E_{\max}\), small \(\nu\), and an \(H^s\) ball containing this family, choose \(k\asymp\log(E_{\max}/\nu)\). Equations (1), (6), and (8) yield the rigorous fixed-coordinate minimax floor
\[
 \text{worst-case }L^2\text{ error}
 \gtrsim [\log(E_{\max}/\nu)]^{-s}.             \tag{9}
\]
This is a specific nonlinear precision barrier, stronger than saying a finite linearization has a kernel. To make the robust absolute error smaller than the response of this pair, normalized readout precision must reach the scale \(k^{-s}r^k\). On an order-one dynamic range, a robust \(b\)-bit accuracy promise therefore needs
\[
 b\gtrsim k\log_2(1/r)+s\log_2k-O(1).          \tag{10}
\]
Equation (10) concerns guaranteed absolute accuracy including calibration bias; it is not a standalone collision theorem for an arbitrarily aligned deterministic quantizer.

Now assume a different, explicitly specified noise model:
\[
 Y_j=Q_\sigma(f_j)+Z_j,\qquad
 Z_j\stackrel{\rm iid}{\sim}N(0,\nu^2),
\]
where \(f_j\) is any measurable function of the previous data
